article.description:
After making numerous miscues down the 
stretch, Sheryl Swoopes buried four clutch free throws to seal
the first victory of the season for the Houston Comets.
article.headline: Comets earn first win since Swoopes' return
article.linkText: Swoopes scores 20 as Comets win first of season
article.story: HOUSTON (AP) -- Sheryl Swoopes scored 20 points and Tynesha Lewis added a career-high 12 as the Houston Comets beat Phoenix 61-56 Wednesday night in the Mercury's WNBA season-opener. Swoopes was 8-for-16 from the field, while the Comets shot just 38 percent. ``Our shots are not falling right now. My shot is not falling right now, but I think we're close to getting to where we want to be,'' said Swoopes, who missed all of last season with a knee injury. Swoopes led the Comets with five steals, including two in the final two minutes. ``My shots might be off right now, but I know that if I get my defense going, the shots are going to start falling,'' she said. Lewis hit two 3-pointers down the stretch for the Comets, who avoided losing two games to start a season for the first time in the franchise's six-year history. ``My teammates did a great job of finding me when I was open,'' Lewis said. ``They were getting double-teamed and they left me open. All I had to do was catch the ball and knock it down.'' Gordana Grubin scored all of her 17 points in the second half for Phoenix, while Jennifer Gillom added 12 and Lisa Harrison had 10. Grubin hit a 3-pointer to pull Phoenix within five points with 10:29 left, but Lewis, who was 5-for-6 from the field, answered with a 3-pointer 25 seconds later. The Mercury pulled within 55-54 with 2:25 remaining, but Houston made six straight free throws to seal the victory. ``I think the Comets have the edge as far as experience is concerned and what to do in the last seconds of a game,'' Phoenix coach Cynthia Cooper said. ``But we were in control of our own fate. We fought back, but we didn't make our layups in the end. Overall, I thought we outplayed them in the second half, but it wasn't enough to win.'' Phoenix committed 11 turnovers in the first half as the Comets took a 28-20 lead behind 10 points from Swoopes. Houston went on an 18-7 run over 7½ minutes to take 28-17 lead. Houston won two of three games from Phoenix last season. The Comets' reserves did not score in Monday's season-opening loss to Los Angeles but had 17 points Wednesday night. ... The Comets are 16-6 all-time against, including 9-1 at Compaq Center.
